statute_title: Driving Under the Influence of Intoxicating Liquor or a Prohibited Substance
offense_class: Misdemeanor (1st/2nd within 7 years); Category B Felony (3rd within 7 years)
elements: Defendant drove or was in actual physical control of a vehicle
While under the influence of intoxicating liquor, a controlled substance, or a combination
Defendant's BAC was .08 or higher, OR driving was impaired by substance
mandatory_minimum: 2 days or 48 hours community service (1st); 10 days residential confinement (2nd); 1 year imprisonment (3rd)
enhancements: Third offense within 7 years (Category B felony)
DUI causing death or substantial bodily harm (NRS § 484C.430)
Prior felony DUI conviction (Category B felony under NRS § 484C.410)
notes: Nevada uses a 7-year lookback period for DUI priors. Implied consent law under NRS § 484C.160. Ignition interlock device required for all DUI convictions. Fourth+ offense or DUI after prior felony DUI is a Category B felony under NRS § 484C.410.

penalty_min: 2 days imprisonment or 48 hours community service
elements: Defendant drove or was in actual physical control of a vehicle
While under the influence of intoxicating liquor or a prohibited substance
BAC of .08 or higher OR impairment demonstrated
No prior DUI conviction within 7 years
mandatory_minimum: Not less than 2 days imprisonment or 48 hours community service
notes: License revoked for 185 days. DUI school and victim impact panel required. Ignition interlock device for 3-6 months.

elements: Defendant drove or was in actual physical control of a vehicle
While under the influence of intoxicating liquor or a prohibited substance
BAC of .08 or higher OR impairment demonstrated
One prior DUI conviction within 7 years
mandatory_minimum: 10 days residential confinement or equivalent community service
notes: License revoked for 1 year. Ignition interlock device required for 12-36 months. Alcohol/drug dependency evaluation required.

elements: Defendant drove or was in actual physical control of a vehicle
While under the influence of intoxicating liquor or a prohibited substance
Two or more prior DUI convictions within 7 years
notes: License revoked for 3 years. State prison sentence mandatory. Eligible for residential confinement program under certain conditions.

statute_title: DUI Causing Death or Substantial Bodily Harm
elements: Defendant drove or was in actual physical control of a vehicle
While under the influence of intoxicating liquor or a prohibited substance
Defendant's driving caused death or substantial bodily harm to another person
notes: This is separate from vehicular homicide charges. License revoked for 3 years. Consecutive sentences possible for multiple victims.

statute_title: Driving Under the Influence of a Controlled Substance (DUID)
elements: Defendant drove or was in actual physical control of a vehicle
While under the influence of a controlled substance or prohibited substance
Substance impaired defendant's ability to safely operate the vehicle
mandatory_minimum: Same as alcohol DUI by offense level
enhancements: Per se limits for specific substances (marijuana, amphetamine, cocaine, etc.)
notes: NRS § 484C.110(4) sets per se blood/urine limits for prohibited substances including marijuana (2 ng/ml blood), cocaine (50 ng/ml urine), heroin (50 ng/ml urine), and methamphetamine (500 ng/ml urine). Same penalty escalation as alcohol DUI.

elements: Defendant unlawfully killed a human being
With premeditation and deliberation, OR
By means of poison, lying in wait, torture, or willful/deliberate/premeditated killing, OR
During the commission of or attempt to commit specified felonies (felony murder)
mandatory_minimum: Life with possibility of parole after 20 years; or 50 years with parole after 20 years
enhancements: Victim was a peace officer, child under 14, or elderly person
notes: Nevada retains the death penalty. Felony murder doctrine applies when killing occurs during robbery, kidnapping, sexual assault, arson, burglary, or certain other felonies.

penalty_max: Life with parole; or 25 years with parole after 10 years
elements: Defendant unlawfully killed a human being
With malice aforethought, express or implied
Without premeditation or deliberation
mandatory_minimum: Life with parole after 10 years; or 25 years with parole after 10 years
notes: All murder which is not first degree murder is second degree murder under NRS § 200.030.

elements: Defendant unlawfully killed a human being
Without malice, express or implied
Upon a sudden heat of passion caused by sufficient provocation
notes: Provocation must be such as would cause a reasonable person to act rashly. Cooling off period negates heat of passion defense.

elements: Defendant caused the death of another human being
Without intent to kill
During the commission of an unlawful act not amounting to a felony, OR
During the commission of a lawful act without due caution or circumspection
notes: Involuntary manslaughter is the unintentional killing of another person during the commission of an unlawful act not amounting to a felony or during the negligent performance of a lawful act.

offense_class: Misdemeanor; Category B Felony (with deadly weapon); Category D Felony (on protected person)
elements: Defendant unlawfully attempted to use physical force against another person, OR
Defendant intentionally placed another person in reasonable apprehension of immediate bodily harm
enhancements: Use of a deadly weapon (Category B felony, 1-6 years)
Victim is a protected person (officer, firefighter, health care provider — Category D felony)
notes: Simple assault is a misdemeanor. Assault with a deadly weapon is always a Category B felony regardless of injury.

offense_class: Misdemeanor; Category B-D Felony depending on circumstances
penalty_max: 6 months (misdemeanor); 1-6 years (Category B with deadly weapon); 1-4 years (Category D on protected person)
elements: Defendant willfully and unlawfully used force or violence upon another person
enhancements: Use of a deadly weapon (Category B felony)
Resulting in substantial bodily harm (Category C felony, 1-5 years)
On a protected person (Category D felony)
notes: Battery is the unlawful touching of another person. No injury required for simple battery. Battery with substantial bodily harm is a Category C felony.

elements: Defendant unlawfully attempted to use physical force against another person OR placed them in reasonable apprehension of immediate bodily harm
Defendant used a deadly weapon in the commission of the assault
enhancements: Victim is a protected person (additional penalties)
notes: A deadly weapon includes any instrument used or threatened to be used in a manner likely to cause death or substantial bodily harm.

elements: Defendant committed a battery
Against a spouse, former spouse, person with whom defendant has/had dating relationship, person related by blood or marriage, co-parent, or custodian/guardian
mandatory_minimum: Not less than 2 days community service (1st); 20 days (2nd); 1 year (3rd+, felony)
enhancements: Strangulation (Category C felony on first offense)
Third or subsequent offense within 7 years (Category C felony)
notes: Firearm prohibition upon conviction under NRS § 202.360. No probation for felony domestic violence. Court must order surrender of firearms. Counseling program required.

penalty_max: Life without parole (with substantial bodily harm)
elements: Defendant willfully seized, confined, inveigled, enticed, decoyed, abducted, concealed, kidnapped, or carried away a person
By any means including force, fraud, or persuasion
With intent to hold for ransom, rob, commit sexual assault, or inflict bodily harm
mandatory_minimum: Life with parole after 5 years (no substantial harm); Life with parole after 15 years (with substantial harm)
notes: First degree kidnapping where victim sustains substantial bodily harm carries life without parole or life with parole after 15 years. Second degree kidnapping (NRS § 200.320) is a Category B felony with 2-15 years.

penalty_max: Life without parole (victim under 14 with substantial bodily harm)
elements: Defendant subjected another person to sexual penetration
Against the will of the victim, OR
Under conditions where the perpetrator knows or should know the victim is mentally or physically incapable of resisting or understanding
mandatory_minimum: Life with parole after 10 years (victim 16+); Life with parole after 25 years (victim 14-15); Life with parole after 35 years (victim under 14)
enhancements: Victim suffered substantial bodily harm (parole eligibility extended)
Victim under 14 with substantial bodily harm (life without parole)
notes: Sexual penetration defined in NRS § 200.364. Includes cunnilingus, fellatio, and any intrusion of any body part or object into genital or anal openings. Sex offender registration required.

elements: Defendant is 18 years or older
Defendant had sexual intercourse with a person 14 or 15 years old
Victim consented (but unable to legally consent due to age)
notes: Age of consent in Nevada is 16. If defendant is under 21 and victim is 14-15, it is a gross misdemeanor. If defendant is 21 or older, it is a Category C felony.

elements: Defendant willfully and lewdly committed any lewd or lascivious act
Upon or with the body of a child under 14 years of age
With the intent of arousing, appealing to, or gratifying the lust, passions, or sexual desires of the defendant or the child
enhancements: Use of force or threat (life without parole)
notes: Sex offender registration required. No statute of limitations for this offense.

elements: Defendant solicited another person to engage in prostitution
In a county where prostitution is not licensed or outside a licensed house of prostitution
notes: Prostitution is legal in certain rural Nevada counties with licensed brothels. Solicitation outside licensed establishments is criminal statewide.

elements: Defendant unlawfully took personal property from the person of another, or in their presence
Against the will of the victim
By means of force or violence or fear of injury, immediate or future
enhancements: Use of a deadly weapon (may double sentence)
notes: Robbery is always a felony in Nevada. Armed robbery with a deadly weapon can carry 2-15 years for the robbery plus additional 1-20 years for the weapon enhancement.

elements: Defendant entered any house, room, apartment, tenement, shop, warehouse, store, mill, barn, stable, outhouse, or other building, tent, vessel, vehicle, vehicle trailer, semitrailer, or house trailer, or airplane
With the intent to commit grand or petit larceny, assault, battery, or any felony
enhancements: Possession of a deadly weapon during burglary (2-15 years)
notes: Entering with intent is sufficient — no need to complete the intended crime. Burglary while in possession of a deadly weapon enhances the penalty range.

elements: Defendant forcibly entered an inhabited dwelling
Without permission of the owner or occupant
With the use of a deadly weapon OR after the use of force upon a person
enhancements: Use of a deadly weapon (2-15 years)
notes: Home invasion is a separate offense from burglary, specifically targeting forcible entry into inhabited dwellings.

offense_class: Category C Felony ($1,200-$5,000); Category B Felony ($5,000-$25,000); Category B Felony ($25,000+)
elements: Defendant intentionally stole, took, and carried away
Personal property of another person
Property valued at $1,200 or more
Without consent of the owner
notes: Grand larceny threshold was raised to $1,200 in 2019. Previously it was $650. Restitution to victim is mandatory in addition to any sentence.

elements: Defendant intentionally stole, took, and carried away
Personal property of another person
Property valued at less than $1,200
Without consent of the owner
enhancements: Prior theft convictions (may elevate to felony)
notes: Petit larceny is a misdemeanor with the $1,200 threshold. Shoplifting under $1,200 is charged as petit larceny. Restitution required.

elements: Defendant knowingly and intentionally took merchandise from a retail establishment
With the intent to permanently deprive the merchant of the merchandise
Without paying the purchase price
enhancements: Use of device to defeat anti-theft measures
notes: Charged under the general theft statute NRS § 205.0832. Civil liability to merchant in addition to criminal penalties.

statute_title: Obtaining and Using Personal Identifying Information of Another Person
elements: Defendant obtained, possessed, or used personal identifying information of another person
Without the authorization of the person
To obtain or attempt to obtain credit, goods, services, or any other thing of value in the name of the other person
notes: Personal identifying information includes SSN, driver's license number, account numbers, passwords, and biometric data. Restitution mandatory.

elements: Defendant falsely made, altered, forged, or counterfeited
Any check, draft, will, deed, bond, or other instrument in writing
With the intent to defraud
notes: Uttering (passing a forged instrument) is a separate offense under NRS § 205.095. Both forgery and uttering carry the same penalty.

statute_title: Fraudulent Use of a Credit or Debit Card
elements: Defendant used a credit card or debit card
Knowing it to be forged, expired, cancelled, revoked, or belonging to another
To obtain money, goods, services, or anything of value
With the intent to defraud
notes: Includes use of credit card numbers without the physical card. Multiple fraudulent transactions may be aggregated.

offense_class: Category E Felony (1st/2nd); Category D Felony (3rd+)
elements: Defendant knowingly or intentionally possessed a controlled substance
Without a valid prescription
Listed in Schedule I, II, III, IV, or V
enhancements: Third or subsequent offense (Category D felony)
notes: First and second offenses are Category E felonies with probation/suspended sentence possible. NRS § 453.3363 allows diversion for first-time possession. Marijuana possession up to 1 oz was legalized in 2017 for adults 21+.

statute_title: Possession of Marijuana — Over Legal Limit
offense_class: Misdemeanor (over 1 oz to 50 lbs); Category E Felony (over 50 lbs)
elements: Defendant possessed marijuana in excess of 1 ounce (28.35 grams)
Without authorization under NRS Chapter 453D
notes: Adults 21+ may possess up to 1 oz of marijuana legally. Possession of 1-50 lbs is a misdemeanor for first offense. Home cultivation limited to 6 plants per person.

statute_title: Possession of Controlled Substance for Sale
offense_class: Category D Felony (Schedule III-V); Category C Felony (Schedule I-II)
elements: Defendant possessed a controlled substance
With the intent to sell, manufacture, or distribute
notes: Intent to sell may be inferred from quantity, packaging, scales, large amounts of cash, or other circumstantial evidence.

offense_class: Category B Felony (Schedule I-II); Category C Felony (Schedule III-V)
elements: Defendant sold, manufactured, delivered, or brought into the state a controlled substance
Without legal authorization
enhancements: Within 1,000 feet of a school (additional penalties)
notes: Sale of Schedule I or II narcotics carries the heaviest penalties. Manufacturing methamphetamine has enhanced penalties.

offense_class: Category B Felony (low quantity); Category A Felony (high quantity)
elements: Defendant knowingly sold, manufactured, delivered, or brought into the state
A controlled substance in specified quantities
100+ grams of Schedule I/II substance (low); 400+ grams (high)
enhancements: Quantity of 400 grams or more (Category A felony, 25 years to life, up to $500,000 fine)
notes: Trafficking thresholds: 100g-400g Schedule I/II is Category B (2-20 years, $100,000); 400g+ is Category A (25 years to life, $500,000). Separate thresholds for marijuana under NRS § 453.339.

statute_title: Possession of Firearm by Prohibited Person
elements: Defendant possessed a firearm
Defendant was a person prohibited from possessing firearms (convicted felon, fugitive, unlawful user of controlled substance, adjudicated mentally ill, subject to domestic violence restraining order)
enhancements: Use of firearm during commission of a crime
notes: Felons may not possess firearms unless pardoned and the pardon does not restrict the right to bear arms. Domestic violence misdemeanor conviction also triggers federal firearms prohibition.

offense_class: Category C Felony (firearm); Gross Misdemeanor (other weapon)
elements: Defendant carried concealed upon their person a weapon
Without a valid CCW permit
Weapon includes firearm, knife with blade over 3 inches, machete, or other dangerous or deadly weapon
notes: Nevada is a shall-issue CCW state. Open carry is legal without a permit. Concealed carry without a permit for a firearm is a Category C felony.

statute_title: Discharging Firearm at or into Occupied Structure or Vehicle
elements: Defendant willfully and maliciously discharged a firearm
At or into any occupied structure, vehicle, aircraft, or watercraft
notes: Structure must be occupied at the time of the shooting. Reckless discharge without targeting an occupied structure may be charged under NRS § 202.285.

elements: Defendant willfully and maliciously set fire to, or caused to be burned
Any dwelling house, structure, or personal property
Whether owned by the defendant or another
enhancements: Occupied structure at time of fire
notes: First degree arson involves occupied dwellings or structures. Second degree arson (NRS § 205.015) involves unoccupied structures and is a Category B felony with 1-10 years. Third degree arson (NRS § 205.020) involves personal property and is a Category D felony.

elements: Defendant took a motor vehicle from the person or presence of another
By means of force, violence, or fear of injury
Against the will of the victim
enhancements: Use of a deadly weapon (additional 1-20 years)
notes: Carjacking is charged under the general robbery statute in Nevada. The use of a deadly weapon adds a consecutive sentence enhancement.

offense_class: Misdemeanor (1st); Gross Misdemeanor (with threat); Category B Felony (with restraining order or prior conviction)
elements: Defendant willfully engaged in a course of conduct directed at a specific person
Which would cause a reasonable person to feel terrorized, frightened, intimidated, or harassed
Defendant actually intended to cause those feelings in the victim
enhancements: Threats of death or substantial bodily harm (gross misdemeanor)
Violation of protective order (Category B felony, 2-15 years)
notes: Cyberstalking is included under this statute. Second or subsequent offense is a gross misdemeanor. Stalking in violation of a restraining order is a Category B felony.

offense_class: Category B Felony (substantial harm/sexual abuse); Gross Misdemeanor (non-substantial harm)
penalty_max: 6 years (non-sexual); 20 years (sexual abuse); Life (death of child)
elements: Defendant willfully caused a child under 18 to suffer unjustifiable physical pain or mental suffering, OR
Placed the child in a situation where the child might suffer physical pain, mental suffering, OR
Physically injured the child in a manner that constituted abuse or neglect
notes: Mandatory reporting requirement for professionals. Gross misdemeanor applies when no substantial bodily harm or mental harm occurs.

elements: Defendant willfully resisted, delayed, or obstructed a public officer
In discharging or attempting to discharge any legal duty of the officer's office
enhancements: Causing bodily harm to the officer
Use of a deadly weapon (separate assault charges)
notes: Does not require physical resistance — verbal obstruction or providing false information can constitute this offense. Flight alone may or may not constitute resistance depending on circumstances.

offense_class: Category D Felony; Category B Felony (causing death or substantial bodily harm)
elements: Defendant operated a motor vehicle
After being given a signal to stop by a peace officer in uniform driving a marked patrol car
Defendant willfully failed or refused to stop
enhancements: Causing death or substantial bodily harm to another (Category B felony, 2-20 years)
notes: The officer must be in a marked vehicle and in uniform. Reckless driving during evasion adds additional charges.

offense_class: Misdemeanor (1st); Gross Misdemeanor (2nd within 2 years); Category D Felony (3rd+ within 2 years)
elements: A valid extended protection order was in effect
Defendant had knowledge of the order
Defendant intentionally violated the terms of the order
enhancements: Third or subsequent within 2 years (Category D felony)
Violation involving assault or battery (separate charges)
notes: Applies to both temporary and extended protection orders for domestic violence, harassment, stalking, and sexual assault.

elements: Defendant knowingly threatened to cause bodily injury to another person
Or to cause physical damage to the property of another
In a manner that would cause a reasonable person to believe the threat was credible
enhancements: Threat with a deadly weapon (assault charges apply separately)
notes: Threats can be made verbally, in writing, or electronically. Distinct from stalking which requires a course of conduct.

elements: Defendant drove a vehicle on a highway
In willful or wanton disregard of the safety of persons or property
enhancements: Causing death or injury (felony charges possible)
notes: Reckless driving is often used as a plea bargain reduction from DUI charges. Points assessed on driving record.

statute_title: Failure to Stop at Scene of Accident — Hit and Run
elements: Defendant was involved in a motor vehicle accident
Defendant failed to immediately stop at the scene
Defendant failed to provide required information or render aid
enhancements: Death of another person (Category B felony, 2-20 years)
Injury to another person (Category B felony, 1-6 years)
notes: Hit and run resulting in death carries 2-20 years imprisonment. If driver was under the influence, DUI charges are added separately.

statute_title: Drawing or Passing a Check Without Sufficient Funds
elements: Defendant willfully drew or passed a check
On a bank or depository
Knowing there were insufficient funds to pay the check
With the intent to defraud
notes: The drawer has 5 days after notification to make the check good. Failure to do so creates a prima facie case of intent to defraud.

elements: Defendant was entrusted with money or property belonging to another
Defendant fraudulently appropriated the money or property to their own use
With the intent to permanently deprive the owner
enhancements: Victim is elderly or vulnerable person
notes: Penalties follow the same value thresholds as grand larceny. Public officer embezzlement carries enhanced penalties.

elements: Defendant knowingly presented or caused to be presented a false or fraudulent claim
For payment or benefit pursuant to an insurance policy
With the intent to defraud
notes: Includes staging accidents, inflating claims, arson for insurance, and falsifying medical records. Restitution mandatory.

elements: Defendant possessed drug paraphernalia

With the intent to use it to plant, propagate, cultivate, grow, harvest, manufacture, compound, convert, produce, process, prepare, test, analyze, pack, repack, store, contain, conceal, inject, ingest, inhale, or otherwise introduce into the human body a controlled substance
enhancements: Sale of paraphernalia to a minor (Category E felony)
notes: Marijuana paraphernalia for personal use by adults 21+ is not a crime. Delivery or sale of paraphernalia to a minor is a Category E felony.

elements: Person is found in a public place
Under the influence of alcohol or a controlled substance
In a condition that creates a danger to self or others
notes: Nevada decriminalized public intoxication under NRS § 458.260. Intoxicated persons are taken to treatment facilities, not arrested. However, disorderly conduct while intoxicated may be charged separately.

elements: Defendant engaged in conduct that disturbed the public peace
Including fighting, violent or tumultuous behavior, or unreasonable noise
notes: Broad statute covering various types of public disturbance. Often used as a lesser included offense or plea reduction.

elements: Defendant went upon the land or into any building of another
After having been warned by the owner or occupant not to trespass, OR
Willfully went or remained on property after being told to leave
notes: Casino trespass is commonly charged when a person is issued a trespass notice from a gaming property and returns.

elements: Defendant willfully disobeyed a lawful order of the court, OR
Engaged in disorderly, contemptuous, or insolent behavior in the presence of the court
notes: Direct contempt may be punished summarily. Indirect contempt requires notice and hearing. Civil contempt is coercive and defendant may purge by compliance.

elements: Defendant was placed on probation for a criminal offense
Defendant violated a condition of probation
Violation was willful and substantial
enhancements: New criminal offense while on probation
notes: Court may revoke probation and impose any sentence originally available. Graduated sanctions may be imposed for technical violations before full revocation.

offense_class: Category B Felony (with deadly weapon); Category D Felony (without)
elements: Defendant restrained the personal liberty of another person
Without sufficient legal authority
enhancements: Use of a deadly weapon (Category B felony, 1-15 years)
notes: False imprisonment without a deadly weapon is a Category D felony. Distinguished from kidnapping by the absence of movement or specific criminal intent.

elements: Defendant was under oath or affirmation
Defendant willfully and knowingly made a false statement
Regarding a material matter
notes: Perjury in a capital case or case involving life imprisonment may carry enhanced penalties. Inconsistent statements under oath can establish perjury without proving which statement was false.

statute_title: Preventing or Dissuading a Witness or Victim
offense_class: Category D Felony; Category B Felony (with force/threat)
penalty_max: 4 years (Cat D); 6 years (Cat B with force)
elements: Defendant knowingly and maliciously prevented or dissuaded any witness or victim
From attending or giving testimony at any trial, proceeding, or inquiry
Or from reporting a crime to law enforcement
enhancements: Use of force or threat (Category B felony)
notes: Includes attempting to prevent a victim from reporting a crime or cooperating with prosecution.

elements: Defendant operated a motor vehicle
In willful or wanton disregard of the safety of persons or property
Causing the death of another person
enhancements: Under the influence of alcohol/drugs (DUI manslaughter charges)
notes: If DUI is involved, the more serious DUI causing death statute (NRS § 484C.430) applies instead. Reckless driving causing death is distinct from involuntary manslaughter.

statute_title: Abuse, Neglect, Exploitation, or Isolation of an Older or Vulnerable Person
offense_class: Gross Misdemeanor (no substantial harm); Category B Felony (substantial harm)
penalty_max: 1 year (gross misd.); 6 years (Cat B); 20 years (Cat B — death result)
elements: Defendant knowingly, willfully, or negligently abused, neglected, exploited, or isolated
An older person (60+) or vulnerable person
Abuse includes physical abuse, financial exploitation, or abandonment
enhancements: Substantial bodily or mental harm (Category B felony)
Death of victim (2-20 years, Category B)
notes: Mandatory reporting requirements for certain professionals. Financial exploitation of elders is prosecuted aggressively under this statute.

offense_class: Gross Misdemeanor (underlying misdemeanor); Category D Felony (underlying felony)
elements: Defendant was released on bail or own recognizance
Defendant willfully failed to appear as required
At a scheduled court hearing or trial
enhancements: Underlying charge is a felony (Category D felony)
notes: Bail jumping is charged in addition to the underlying offense. Court will issue a bench warrant upon failure to appear.

offense_class: Varies (same class as target offense; Category B felony for murder/manslaughter/robbery/sexual assault conspiracy)
penalty_max: Same as target offense; 6 years (specific violent felonies)
elements: Two or more persons agreed to commit a crime
At least one person performed an overt act in furtherance of the agreement
enhancements: Target offense is a violent felony
notes: Conspiracy to commit murder, robbery, kidnapping, or sexual assault is a Category B felony (1-6 years). Conspiracy to commit other crimes is punished at the same level as the target offense.

statute_title: Battery on a Protected Person (Officer, Firefighter, etc.)
offense_class: Category D Felony; Category B Felony (with substantial bodily harm)
penalty_max: 4 years (Cat D); 6 years (Cat B with substantial harm)
elements: Defendant willfully and unlawfully used force or violence
Upon a peace officer, firefighter, school employee, health care provider, or other protected person
While the protected person was performing their duties
enhancements: Substantial bodily harm (Category B felony, 2-10 years)
notes: Protected persons include officers, firefighters, judges, providers of health care, school employees, and child protective services workers. Separate from general battery statute.

elements: Defendant committed any act of open or gross lewdness
In a public place or where others could observe
notes: Includes indecent exposure and public sexual acts. First offense is a gross misdemeanor; subsequent offenses are Category D felonies. Sex offender registration may be required.

elements: Defendant willfully and maliciously destroyed or damaged property
Belonging to another person
notes: Restitution for repair or replacement of damaged property is mandatory in addition to any sentence.

offense_class: Category B Felony (with force/threat of force); Category D Felony (without force)
elements: Defendant compelled another person to do or abstain from doing an act
By means of force, threat of force, or intimidation
Which the person had a right to do or abstain from doing
enhancements: Use of force or threat of force (Category B felony)
notes: Coercion with force or threat of force is a Category B felony (1-6 years). Without force, it is a Category D felony (1-4 years). Commonly charged in domestic violence contexts.

elements: Defendant bought, received, possessed, or withheld property
Knowing the property was stolen
With the intent to deprive the owner of the property
notes: Value thresholds match grand larceny thresholds. Knowledge that property was stolen may be inferred from circumstances.

statute_title: Failure to Register as Sex Offender
offense_class: Category D Felony (1st); Category C Felony (subsequent)
elements: Defendant was required to register as a sex offender
Defendant failed to register or update registration as required
Failure was willful
notes: Registration is lifetime for Tier III offenders. Must register within 48 hours of establishing residence or changing address.

offense_class: Varies (one category lower than completed offense)
elements: Defendant had the specific intent to commit a crime
Defendant performed a direct but ineffectual act toward the commission of the crime
notes: Attempt is generally punished one category below the completed offense (e.g., attempt of a Category B is Category C). Exception: attempted murder is a Category B felony (2-20 years).
